title: Settlement double-posting under retry
body:
Status: Closed (fixed)
Reporter: Lena Fischer
Assignee: Raj Patel

During v2.5 staging tests we reproduced a case where a settlement is applied twice when the settler retries after a timeout. The idempotency protection described in ADR-004 is not being enforced on this path, so the retry posts a second entry. This is a release blocker for the v2.5 settlement work (PAY-501) — we should not ship until the key is enforced and verified in staging.

Comment (Raj Patel): Confirmed the applied-key check was being skipped for the async settler path. Fix in progress.
Comment (Lena Fischer): Re-tested after the fix — retries are now no-ops. Verified in staging.
author: Lena Fischer

blocked-by: LED-412

title: RCA: duplicate charges in production (June 3)
body:
Status: Resolved
Incident date: 2026-06-03
Assignee: Maya Chen

Timeline: A subset of customers were charged twice within a short window. Charges correlated with a spike in Risk Engine scoring timeouts, which led the payment path to retry (see RISK-220). Under normal conditions a retry should be harmless.

Investigation: We are reviewing recent changes to the settlement hot path; a recent performance-oriented change is under review as a contributing factor. Corrective action tracked in PAY-540.

Comment (Arjun Rao): The retries themselves are expected behavior under timeouts; the open question is why a retry resulted in a second charge.
author: Maya Chen

title: Risk Engine scoring timeouts under load; add client retry
body:
Status: Done
Assignee: Marco Rossi

Under peak load the inline scoring client (see ADR-002) intermittently exceeds its latency budget and times out, causing payment authorizations to fail. To improve resilience we added a retry on timeout in the scoring client on the payment side.

Comment (Marco Rossi): Retry on timeout deployed. This reduces user-facing auth failures during Risk slowness.
author: Marco Rossi

title: RCA: duplicate notifications (June 9)
body:
Status: Resolved
Incident date: 2026-06-09
Assignee: Tom Nguyen

Timeline: Customers received duplicate receipt notifications. The notification consumer reads from the at-least-once event bus (ADR-003), so the same event can be delivered more than once. Under normal operation the consumer should collapse redeliveries.

Investigation: A recent change to the consumer is under review as a contributing factor. Corrective action tracked in NOT-320.

Comment (Hana Kim): Redelivery is expected on this bus; the question is why redeliveries were no longer being collapsed.
author: Tom Nguyen

title: Notification batching release
body:
Status: In progress (behind schedule)
Assignee: Hana Kim

Batch low-priority notifications to reduce send volume. Target was early June.

Comment (Tom Nguyen): We are behind on this. The team was pulled onto an urgent dedup fix (NOT-320) following the June 9 incident, and batching work is paused until that lands.
Comment (Hana Kim): Will resume once NOT-320 ships.
author: Hana Kim

title: Revert recent settlement hot-path change
body:
Status: Done
Assignee: Arjun Rao
Parent: PAY-530

Comment (Arjun Rao): Reverted the implicated change on the settlement hot path. Verified that retries no longer produce a second charge.
author: Arjun Rao

title: Re-add deduplication to notification consumer
body:
Status: Done
Assignee: Hana Kim
Parent: NOT-310

Follow-up to the June 9 incident. A recent consumer refactor removed the deduplication step; restore idempotent dedup by event id so at-least-once redeliveries are collapsed.

Comment (Hana Kim): Dedup restored and verified against replayed events. This pulled the team off the batching work (NOT-300).
